newsitem.title: UK: Buckingham Palace to campaign for Charles as king.
newsitem.headline: Buckingham Palace to campaign for Charles as king.

text.p: Buckingham Palace will launch a five-year campaign to try to persuade dubious Britons that Prince Charles is fit to be the country's king one day, the Daily Mail reported on Thursday.

The newspaper said the palace took the decision after a television poll on Tuesday showed Charles had slumped in popularity after his acrimonious divorce from Princess Diana last year and his adulterous affair with old flame Camilla Parker Bowles.

"With support for the royal family seriously weakened by what are perceived to be the Prince's personal failings, his behaviour is now at the heart of the monarchy's future," the Daily Mail said in a front-page report.
The palace would concentrate on selling Charles's good deeds rather than trying to remake his image, a policy which had failed in the past, it said.

The pivotal point of the new plan would be the year 2002, when Queen Elizabeth would celebrate 50 years on the throne and then start handing over some of her duties as head of state to Charles. But there would be no question of her abdicating.
Earlier this week another tabloid newspaper quoted Charles as admitting he had failed the monarchy. The prince vowed to "sort the whole bloody mess out" by reaching out more to ordinary people.
Charles is believed to want to mend fences, at least in public, with the popular Princess Diana, the mother of their two sons Prince William, 14, and Prince Harry, 12.

In another populist move, Charles has signalled he wants to play a greater role in the Church of England, of which he will be head when he takes the throne. He has toned down his outspoken remarks in favour of other religions.
